card.name: Not applicable (NA) entries in tables
card.fires_on: The spot just before or at an abbreviation meaning not applicable or not available, such as NA or na in table legends, or a quote mark before a 'negative' or 'none' style entry. It is most often seen in drug interaction and dilution tables.

modes.label: NA legend
modes.description: Punctuation or the abbreviation NA/na itself in a table key defining NA as not applicable or not calculated.
modes.example: ↔ = No change (↑ or ↓ less than 10%);<< NA>> = C min not calculated for single-d

modes.label: Placeholder value slot
modes.description: A spot where a missing or null value could be written, like a quote before a recorded result or a word starting 'Not Applicable'.
modes.example: The absence of induration should be recorded as "0 mm" not<< ">>negative".

card.writes: It pushes the model toward writing unknown, NA or not-available placeholders.
card.plain: It fires where a table says a value is not applicable or unknown, such as NA in a key.
